claim: Bounded compatibility on a previously inspected cohort; not a proof of rules correctness.

proposal.hypothesis: Game 18 ran out of its 10000-node budget at user turn 3. The cause was in the search, not the engine. The search only compared a turn against the recording at its end-of-turn boundary, so a branch that was already hopeless in the middle of a turn still explored every later action in that turn. The baseline rejections show this: 404 branches cast Last Gasp as well as Impractical Joke (recorded: only Impractical Joke), each found only at end of turn. The retained trace shows the recorded line is reachable in the engine: draw Forum of Amity, play Mountain, Impractical Joke kills the 5/3 Stone Docent (two +1/+1 counters, which hit for 5 on opponent turn 3), and Shattered Acolyte attacks unblocked for 2 with lifelink (life 17 and 18). Within a turn the per-turn observation lists (drawn, land_played, creature_cast, non_creature_cast, instant_sorcery_cast, drawn_or_tutored_count) only grow. progress.events is cleared only when a turn starts. So once a list holds more copies of a name than the recorded multiset, or more entries than the recorded count, no continuation of that turn can pass the end-of-turn comparison.
risks: Pruning is sound only while progress.events stays append-only within a turn and the end-of-turn comparison stays a multiset or count equality on these projections. A future projection that removes entries mid-turn, or compares with a looser rule, would need to be left out of exceeded_turn_field.

The pruning changes the depth-first visit order. It could in principle change which of several valid witnesses is found first, though every reported witness still passes the full end-of-turn comparisons.
proposal.summary: Added exceeded_turn_field in fitting/search.rs. After each accepted action it checks the enforced fields of the active player's current turn and rejects the branch as soon as the turn's progress exceeds a recorded multiset or count. The rejection is tallied as 'exceeded_before_eot'. Only enforced fields with an expected value are used. Unsupported or blank fields never prune. The end-of-turn comparison itself is unchanged and still decides every match. No budgets, fields or boundary rules changed. Added the unit test turn_progress_beyond_a_recorded_multiset_or_count_is_rejected_early. It covers multiset overflow, count overflow, that unsupported fields don't prune, and that only the active player's current turn is constrained. I also tried counting the cleanup events ManaPoolEmptied and DamageCleared as neutral at the turn boundary. The matched witness for game 18 does not need that, so I reverted it to keep the change to the one cause I verified.
proposal.validation: Full ./try: format, lint and tests pass. Game 18 went from budget_exhausted 10/12 (10000 nodes) to matched_supported_projection 12/12 (4339 nodes): newly matched. No game regressed. The other 10 matched games still match 12/12. Games 02, 06 and 11 need fewer nodes (1989->1861, 460->360, 2634->995). The rest are unchanged. The 9 mulligan input-issue games are unchanged. Gate result: passed True, improved 1, regressed 0.

reason: Tests pass, at least one game improved, none regressed, and the reviewer approved.

findings: The prune is general and tied to the claimed cause: it rejects a branch only when an enforced, current-turn field already exceeds its recorded multiset or count, and it names no game or card.
It weakens no check: the end-of-turn comparison is untouched and still decides every match, and unsupported, blank or non-array expectations never prune.

Soundness rests on two things I could not confirm from the diff alone: that `progress.events` is append-only within a turn, and that the end-of-turn comparison is exact multiset/count equality on the same un-normalised names that `progress.list` returns.
The gate result plausibly follows from the change: game 18 is newly matched under the same 10000-node budget, the other 10 matched games still match 12/12, and node counts only fall.

The contributor's node counts do not match the gate's (game 18: 4339 vs 4218; game 02: 1861 vs 1981; game 06: 360 vs 356), so their validation was probably run on a different revision, perhaps before the cleanup-event revert.
The unit test covers multiset overflow, count overflow, unsupported fields and turn scoping, but not a mid-turn boundary crossing where the active player changes on the pruned action.
review.summary: The change is a monotonicity-based early rejection that addresses the stated cause without touching budgets, fields or the end-of-turn comparison, and the gate shows one new match with no regressions. I reviewed only the diff and gate output, not the surrounding code, so the append-only and exact-equality invariants are taken from the proposal. The node-count mismatch should be reconciled, but the gate's own numbers support keeping the change.
